metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

evidence: Approach: 'The differ keys on `landed_text`'; 'landed_text = strip_marker(codec.decode_inbound(codec.to_wire(wire_body)))'
AC-1: 'asserts key == hash(wire_body) == hash(what the fake transport received)'
Current Jira-side key at outbound_comments.py:591-594 is `_normalize_comment_body(codec.to_wire(decorate(fit_comment(body))))` — decoded and marker-stripped, matching `landed_text`, NOT `wire_body`
wire_body per Approach = `fit_preserving_marker(decorate(body), fit)` — a decorated, marker-bearing string, not the decoded key
findings.finding: AC-1 asserts the dedup key equals `hash(wire_body)`, but the Approach defines the differ key as `landed_text` (the marker-STRIPPED decoded readback of `to_wire(wire_body)`), and `wire_body` is the marker-BEARING pre-encode text — so `hash(wire_body)` cannot equal the key or the Jira-side inbound key, which is the decoded/stripped form. The acceptance oracle contradicts the keying mechanism.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria line 1 vs Approach (`landed_text`/`wire_body` definitions)
findings.suggested_fix: Change AC-1 to assert `key == landed_text == strip_marker(decode(what the fake transport received))`, keeping the key symmetric with the Jira-side `_normalize_comment_body(to_wire(fetched))` inbound key rather than hashing the marker-bearing `wire_body`.

evidence: 'checked by `git diff --stat`'
DC backend.py is listed in Scope and will change (fit_comment delegation), so its appearance in diff --stat is expected and uninformative about the 32767 prose
findings.finding: AC8 proves the sourced 32767 occurrences are unchanged via `git diff --stat`, but --stat reports per-file changed-line counts, not whether a specific literal survived. DC `backend.py` IS in scope (fit_comment delegation), so it will legitimately appear in the diff — --stat cannot distinguish 'prose/32767 unchanged' from 'prose changed'.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, line 8 ('The sourced 32767 occurrences ... unchanged; checked by git diff --stat')
findings.suggested_fix: Assert the 32767 count per protected file is unchanged with an anchored grep (`grep -oE '32767' <file> | wc -l` == expected N) rather than relying on diff --stat granularity.

evidence: Plan: '`32767` occurs in FOUR files under `src/rebar/_engine`'

grep '32767' under src/rebar/_engine returns FIVE files: runtime.py:46, jira_datacenter/backend.py (244/246/248/257), jira_datacenter/settings.py (60/64), jira/comment_limits.py:41, and jira_family/rich_text.py:60
rich_text.py:60 `WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT: int = 32767` — DC text-field cap, a sourced limit like the others, in the owner module the plan edits
The sourced-32767 AC ('unchanged; checked by git diff --stat') names only runtime.py, DC settings.py and DC backend.py — neither the constraint nor the AC accounts for the rich_text.py:60 occurrence
findings.finding: The Constraint 'the sourced 32767 occurrences must SURVIVE' asserts '32767 occurs in FOUR files under src/rebar/_engine' and enumerates exactly four (comment_limits.py:41, runtime.py:46, DC settings.py:60,64, DC backend.py:244-257), but a grep finds a FIFTH occurrence at adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py:60 (`WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT: int = 32767`) — in the very owner module the plan makes the single home for the truncation suffix. The exhaustive-count premise is factually wrong.
findings.location: Constraint: the sourced `32767` occurrences must SURVIVE
findings.suggested_fix: Change 'FOUR files' to 'FIVE files' and add a bullet for `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py:60` `WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` (DC text-field cap, sourced from the same documented 32,767 limit); extend the sourced-32767 acceptance criterion's git diff --stat guard to include rich_text.py's limit line (distinct from its suffix-literal line, which the plan does edit).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the send-time encode rule with AC4: state whether wire_body is written verbatim (codec invoked once, by fit_for_send) OR re-encoded with the same instance at send (codec invoked twice), and make AC4's cardinality match the chosen path per adapter.
evidence: 'The send path MUST NOT re-encode: it writes wire_body verbatim.'
'Where an adapter genuinely must encode at send time, it receives the same codec instance fit_for_send was given, asserted by an identity test'
AC4: 'add_comment performs no independent fit/encode; checked by a test asserting a fake codec is invoked exactly once per outbound comment.'
findings.finding: The 'one codec, one set of bytes' constraint contains two sentences in tension: 'The send path MUST NOT re-encode: it writes wire_body verbatim' versus 'Where an adapter genuinely must encode at send time, it receives the same codec instance'. AC4 then asserts the codec is 'invoked exactly once per outbound comment', which a send-time re-encode would violate (fit_for_send call + send-time call = two invocations).
findings.location: Constraint: one codec, one set of bytes / Acceptance Criteria AC4
scenarios: Executor must decide whether the DC send path re-encodes wire_body (invoking codec a second time) or writes bytes verbatim; the exactly-once assertion and the 'may encode at send time' allowance point opposite ways.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify that wire_body is transport-ready bytes written verbatim (codec invoked exactly once, inside fit_for_send), and reframe the 'must encode at send time' clause as: if any adapter cannot carry pre-encoded bytes, it re-encodes wire_body with the SAME injected codec instance and AC4 counts that path as one fit + one verbatim re-encode — pick one and align the exactly-once wording.
